general.purpose: QuantumPath is a quantum software development platform intended to support the design, implementation, and execution of quantum software applications. The authors present it as an agnostic platform and ecosystem of tools, services, and processes to simplify development of quantum algorithms and their integration into hybrid information systems.

source_type.evidence: Although it is not open-source software, it can be accessed in a very advantageous way if you are part of theaQuantum network,

type_evidence.evidence: The annealer compositor is a high-level tool that allows one to model optimisation problems in a fully graphical andvisual way (Figure 4), without needing to use any programming language.

With the Direct Code feature a specialist in the quantum vendor's specific technologies can enter code in the vendor's ownlanguage (qASM in the case of QISKIT, Python OCEAN in the case of D-Wave Ocean, etc.).
The corresponding metalanguage is then transpiled in design time to the program-ming language supported by each manufacturer and executed in the target environment.
Using this dashboard allows us to coordinate the necessary executions and checkthe results,
For this purpose, as shown in Figure 2, QuantumPath collects in its telemetry system database alarge amount of data on the different executions of the programs on different systems,

automation_level.evidence: The QuantumPath CORE, through its process manager, will be responsible for carrying out all the necessary actionsto respond to the user's needs and to provide the different consolidated results.

evaluation_type.evidence: A more complete demonstration, walking the user through two examples of quantum-gates based circuit design andannealing-based optimisation, can be found in the aQuantum YouTube channel.

architecture.design_principles: Agnostic support for both gate-based and annealing quantum technology; integration of quantum/classical hybrid information systems; independence from specific platforms and languages via “write once, run everywhere”; use of proprietary metalanguages transpiled to vendor languages; support for quantum software lifecycle and engineering.
architecture.technological_foundation: Quirk Quantum Circuit Simulator; REST API services; qASM; Python OCEAN; QISKIT; Ocean; Q#; Jupyter notebook; GitHub.

orchestrator.evidence: The flow has the responsibility for ensuring the coordination between the circuits and all the elements in which QuantumPath will be executed.

manager_controller.evidence: The QuantumPath CORE, through its process manager, will be responsible for carrying out all the necessary actions to respond to the user's needs and to provide the different consolidated results.

vendor_agnostic_layer.evidence: both the circuit editor and the annealing editor generate a proprietary metalanguage that is agnostic to each vendor's quantum technology.

backend_integration.evidence: This backend manages the approved connections of quantum simulators and quantum computers to suppliers;

debugging_testing.evidence: Tools for the design, construction, testing and execution of quantum assets from the context of both agnostic and platform-specific solutions:

simulation_support.evidence: QuantumPath allows the user to work with different quantum technologies such as those from IBM, Microsoft, Rigetti, D-Wave, Google and Fujitsu, as well as with third-party quantum computing simulators such as QuTECH or CTIC.

security_mechanisms.evidence: All the data elements stored in the cloud system are stored encrypted from origin to storage,

scalability_mechanisms.evidence: A backend that - by design - contemplates security, high availability, load balancing and asynchronous customer processing.

telemetry_monitoring.evidence: and will also collect all the telemetry from the process,

user_interface.evidence: The circuit editor permits the graphical design of quantum gate circuits (Figure 3) through a web user interface (UI)

challenges.statement: QuantumPath has required modifications because integrated external tools release incompatible versions and discontinue features.
challenges.category_evidence: "Several of the tools we have integrated into QuantumPath have been released in different versions (not always compatible with the previous ones), and some features have been discontinued - with the result that we have had to modify our platform."
challenges.strength_evidence: "Several of the tools we have integrated into QuantumPath have been released in different versions (not always compatible with the previous ones), and some features have been discontinued - with the result that we have had to modify our platform."

challenges.statement: Providing integrated design services for both gate-based quantum and annealing systems on the same platform has been difficult.
challenges.category_evidence: "Design services for both gate-based quantum and annealing systems have been difficult to offer on the same platform and in an integrated manner."
challenges.strength_evidence: "Design services for both gate-based quantum and annealing systems have been difficult to offer on the same platform and in an integrated manner."

challenges.statement: QuantumPath still lacks capabilities needed to fully support software engineering, leaving substantial work remaining.
challenges.category_evidence: "we still have a lot of work ahead of us if we are to turn the QuantumPath platform into a platform that truly supports software engineering."
challenges.strength_evidence: "we still have a lot of work ahead of us if we are to turn the QuantumPath platform into a platform that truly supports software engineering."

challenges.statement: QuantumPath does not yet include facilities for re-engineering quantum software, including transformation from classical to quantum software and migration between gate-based and annealing paradigms.
challenges.category_evidence: "Integrating facilities for the re-engineering of quantum software,34 which would allow on the one hand the transformation from classical to quantum software, and on the other the migration of quantum software from the gate-based paradigm to the annealing paradigm."

challenges.statement: QuantumPath still needs tools to assure quantum software quality, including testing and quality metrics.
challenges.category_evidence: "Developing a set of tools to assure quantum software quality, both as regards the testing and the metrics for quantum software quality (maintainability, performance, etc.)."

challenges.statement: The platform still needs validation on increasingly complex problems and industry-scale performance assurance.
challenges.category_evidence: "Testing the platform with increasingly complex problems and assuring an agreed industry scale performance (as far as the underlying quantum hardware allows this)."

challenges.statement: QuantumPath's telemetry system still needs improvement and tuning to better evaluate hardware and optimize reliable execution.
challenges.category_evidence: "Improving and tuning the telemetry system of QuantumPath, in order to evaluate quantum hardware and to optimise quantum programs that can be executed with high reliability on existing quantum hardware, following the proposal of Reference 35."

challenges.statement: QuantumPath does not yet incorporate quantum error correction tools to handle noisy bits and related problems.
challenges.category_evidence: "Incorporating in the platform some quantum error correction (QEC) tools36 to deal with noisy bits and the problems they can cause."
